subject: Mutual action timetable & QBR coordination — Brightline renewal
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@brightline.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action timetable & QBR coordination — Brightline renewal

Hi Sara —

Hope you’re well. With Brightline’s current term coming up at the end of September, I wanted to kick off a short renewal coordination thread so we can align on timeline, capacity needs, and the QBR slot. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm target term change (12 vs 24 months) and any required budget approvals on your side.
- Share a short list of expected throughput changes for Q3–Q4 so we can size Reserved capacity and propose cost options (I attached a simple forecast template).
- Propose two QBR windows in Sept for executive presence: week of Sep 9 or Sep 16 (we’ll hold ~90 minutes).

I’ve looped in Soojin (CS) for onboarding/staffing, Lauren (SE) for technical ramp/runbook, and Jonas (AE) for any commercial nuances. If helpful, I can send a mutual action plan draft after we pick a QBR slot and confirm the term.

Next step: could you share any internal procurement windows and 3 potential QBR slots by end of week?

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on a smooth renewal.

—Michael Grant
Head of Account Strategy, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity-forecast-2028Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)
From: Sara Patel <sara@brightline.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightline.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action timetable & QBR coordination — Brightline renewal

Michael —

Thanks for the kickoff. Quick answers:

1) Term: leaning toward a 24-month commitment but need final approval from procurement and finance.
2) Throughput: our volume forecast for tokens is expected to increase ~35% in Q4 given a new feature launch; I filled the attached high-level numbers and included a peak-day multiplier.
3) QBR windows: both weeks look OK — our execs prefer Sep 16 (Thu) 10:00–11:30 PT or Sep 18 (Mon) 14:00–15:30 PT.

Procurement asked for proposed commercial language on seat-based pricing vs throughput tiers and a brief note on data residency controls (we are EU+US customers). Can you share a cost comparison we can give finance?

Cc’ing Procurement. We’ll confirm term once procurement runs the internal DSC by mid-June.

Best,
Sara Patel
Director of Product, Brightline
sara@brightline.ai
Attachment: brightline-forecast-filled.csv (CSV, 8 KB)

Thanks Michael / Sara — I can take point on the mutual action plan and run the staffing estimates. Tentative internal plan from CS/RAM:

- If Brightline confirms +35% Q4 volume and commits by end of Sept, we’ll need +2 dedicated GPUs in Q4 ramp (likely Redwood Dedicated pool) and 1 additional CS engineer for the first 6 weeks of onboarding.
- Lauren: can you validate runbook hours for a daylight cutover for the new throughput?
- Jonas: can you prepare two commercial options for Sara’s procurement team — (A) 24-month seat + throughput buffer, (B) 12-month throughput-tier with seasonal burst credits. Include delta to current ARR.

I attached a mutual action plan draft — I’ll iterate once Sara confirms the QBR. Proposed next steps for internal owners:

1) Lauren: technical validation & runbook estimate (due Tue 6/12).
2) Jonas: commercial options & draft language for procurement (due Wed 6/13).
3) Michael: confirm exec QBR invite and attendee list; I’ll draft the kickoff agenda.

Soojin Lee

Sara / Procurement —

Great — thanks for the clarity. To keep momentum I’ve booked the QBR for Sep 16, 10:00–11:30 PT (calendar invite to follow) and pulled together two commercial sketches for procurement to review (seat vs throughput). Jonas will drop the formal comparison by 6/13, and Lauren will confirm the runbook hours by 6/12.

I also included a DocuSign link for a placeholder LOI (non-binding) so procurement can see commercial guardrails ahead of the DSC. We’ll treat this as a planning artifact; final terms will land in the order form.

Action items recap:
- Procurement: review high-level options (Jonas to send 6/13).
- Lauren: runbook & technical hours (due 6/12).
- Soojin: final mutual action plan update after the above.
- Michael: finalize QBR agenda and confirm exec list by 6/14.

Thanks all — we’ll reconvene if any of the above slips.

—Michael Grant
